html:
A rush of some 300,000 people to California after gold was found at Sutter's Mill in January 1848. The find came days before Mexico signed California over to the United States at the end of the war between the two countries.

Word spread in 1848, and in 1849 the "forty-niners" poured in by land over the overland trails, by sea around Cape Horn and across Panama, where the Panama Railroad was later built for them. They came from the eastern US and also from Chile, Mexico, Europe, Australia and China.

The results:

  • San Francisco grew from a village of about a thousand people to a city.
  • California became a state in 1850, without slavery.
  • California's Native peoples were devastated by disease, starvation and killings, some paid for by the state.
  • Chinese and Mexican miners faced special taxes and violence, an early step toward the Chinese Exclusion Act.

Easy surface gold ran out within a few years and mining passed to companies. Gold seekers moved on to new rushes, such as the Victorian gold rush in Australia from 1851.
sum: A rush of some 300,000 people to California after gold was found at Sutter's Mill in January 1848. The find came days before Mexico signed California over to the United States at the end of the war between the two countries.
